Later, a company copies her formulation and starts commercial production. Ananya approaches the authorities claiming exclusive rights over her invention.
Which of the following is the most appropriate legal position regarding Ananya’s claim for patent protection ?
(A)  She cannot claim protection because patents are applicable only to artistic works.
(B)  She can claim patent rights because the invention is useful and scientific.
(C)  She can claim patent rights because publication strengthens ownership.

A public library introduces a rule that senior citizens above the age of
60 years will be given free membership, while others are required to pay a nominal fee. A group of library users challenge the rule, claiming it violates their right to equality.
Which of the following best reflects the correct legal position under Article 14 of the Constitution of India ?
(A)  The rule is valid because it applies uniformly to all persons above the age of 60 years.
(B)  The rule is valid because the difference in treatment is based on a reasonable basis and serves a legitimate purpose.
(C)  The rule is invalid because equality requires identical treatment of all persons.

Identify the correct legal classification of the property involved in the above transactions.
(A)  Both the sugarcane and the teak tree are immovable properties.
(B)  Sugarcane is an immovable property and the teak tree is a movable property.
(C)  Sugarcane is a movable property and the teak tree is an immovable property until cut.
(D)  Both sugarcane and the teak tree are movable properties.

Mr. Sharma had not given any permission for this. While taking the measurements, Mr. Kapoor accidentally stepped on some flower beds and caused minor damage. When confronted, Mr. Kapoor argued that he was only measuring his own property and did not intend any harm.
Which of the following statements is correct regarding Mr. Kapoor’s actions ?
(A) Mr. Kapoor has committed trespass to land, because he entered Mr.
Sharma’s property without consent.
(B) Mr. Kapoor cannot be held liable since his intention was not to harm Mr. Sharma.
(C) Minor damage to the flower beds makes the act insignificant and not legally actionable.

(B) Article 20 – Protection of rights of persons accused of crimes.

(D) Article 22 – Safeguards against arbitrary arrest and detention.
